data.narrative:
Astro Mechanica is a Series A-stage company in the Supersonic & Hypersonic sector, founded by Ian Brooke and having raised $27M+ to date. The addressable comp universe consists of four identified peers: two public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and two private players (Boom Supersonic, Hermeus). The narrow peer set in this frontier segment limits traditional comparable company analysis.

Given data constraints, the Stage-Progression method provides the primary quantitative anchor. Using $27M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression to subsequent stages yields an implied valuation of $54M. This method is applicable because it directly references observed fund deployment and standard venture step-up patterns, though it carries inherent limitations in a pre-revenue or early-revenue frontier-tech context where capital raise amounts do not necessarily correlate tightly with value creation.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables in the Supersonic & Hypersonic vertical—fewer than the three minimum datapoints required for statistical reliability. Drawing on the broader public comp set would introduce excessive heterogeneity and skew results.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $46M (low) to $62M (high), with a median point of $54M. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow peer valuation data, the pre-commercial or nascent-revenue status typical of hypersonic ventures, and execution risk inherent to hardware-stage companies. This range reflects method limitations rather than high confidence.
